previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, gastroparesis, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for right lower quadrant abdominal pain. Initial evaluation showed mild tenderness without signs of acute abdomen. Imaging revealed no evidence of obstruction, inflammation, or appendicitis. Her elevated creatinine improved with IV hydration, attributed to poor oral intake. A colonoscopy was unremarkable, though the terminal ileum was poorly visualized. She experienced a brief episode of bright red blood per rectum, with a small, stable hemoglobin drop, attributed to internal hemorrhoids. Pain resolved with supportive care, including bowel regimen and metoclopramide. She was discharged home with improved symptoms, a plan for outpatient GI follow-up, and continuation of a bowel regimen and metoclopramide, with instructions to monitor for medication interactions and recurrent symptoms.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled

All her labs and physical exam were unremarkable, and had undergone extensive workup for her abdominal pain in the past and during her last admission, so was discharged home with close followup. # Chronic abdominal pain: The patient was admitted for abdominal pain, nausea, and lightheadedness. Orthostatic vital signs were checked twice and were negative for any orthostatic hypotension. Abdominal exam remained benign with good bowel sounds, no rebound/guarding, and normal well-formed bowel movements. Nausea subsided with PO ondansetron and patient was able to eat a full breakfast and lunch. Patient was really admitted in ___ for similar complaint and was found to have negative CT Abdomen x 2 and negative colonoscopy, although with incomplete prep. The case was discussed with the patient's outpatient gastroenterologist, Dr. ___ will see her soon in follow-up. Her LFTs, CBC, and CHEM 7 were normal, and rectal exam showed guiac-negative stool and regular BMs. Her pain improved over the course of the day and she was transitioned from IV morphine to her home PO regimen of tizanidine and Tylenol. Due to these findings and recent negative imaging, the decision was made not to pursue repeat imaging at this time. She was given 1 L IVF overnight and was discharged on her home abdominal pain regimen of Reglan, Zofran, Ativan, Tizanidine, and Omeprazole. She will see Dr. ___ in follow-up next week. Dr. ___ that he may recommend outpatient repeat colonoscopy in the future. # Diabetes: The patient's diabetes remained well-controlled during this hospitalization on an insulin sliding scale. # Hypertension: The patient's blood pressures were well-controlled on her home medications of amlodipine and lisinopril. No changes were made to her BP medication regime. She will follow-up with her primary care physician. # Depression: The patient missed her recent psychiatry appointment due to a migraine, but is scheduled to follow-up with her psychiatrist, her counselor, and her chronic pain physician within the next 4 weeks.
